key_insight: QSTAR shows that quantum heads are most valuable as selective fallback branches for uncertain inputs, not as uniform replacements for classical classifiers.
engineering_relevance: For hybrid AI systems, confidence-based routing can improve robustness and deployment efficiency by reserving quantum computation for only the hardest samples.
method: Compare manual QTL heads, KetGPT-designed quantum heads, and parameter-matched classical baselines
Route low-confidence predictions to a fallback branch using adaptive thresholds
evidence_signal: On the shared evaluation setup, the strongest KetGPT head reached 78.5% accuracy and 0.785 F1, while Adaptive KetGPT-QTL reached 80.9% accuracy and 0.807 F1.
watch_item: The gains depend on confidence-threshold tuning and the reported benefits come from a single dataset/backbone setup, so generalization remains uncertain.
paper_title: QSTAR: Quantum Selective Transfer with Adaptive Routing
